rationale: A wins because it keeps five genuinely different doors open without pretending the missing facts are already proven. Its best move is the accountability frame, "Klarna won't say how many of the jobs it cut were actually replaced by AI," which names the tension instead of decorating it. B has strong bones, but "the Equivalent of 700 People Are Gone" and "The Headcount It Cut Is the Margin It's Showing Investors" overstate the record by blurring FTE-equivalent work, attrition, unfilled roles, and actual cuts.
gaps_in_A: "The most-mocked category of enterprise AI might actually be working" is a little cute and rests on an asserted industry premise that is plausible but not in the supplied facts.
"The IPO filing is the live event" is directionally supported, but A should be more careful: the facts say Klarna has filed to go public, not that a fresh S-1 passage contains these AI metrics.

The consumer angle says "AI is now handling disputes" when the update only says consumer advocates raised concerns about AI handling disputes; that needs softer wording unless Klarna confirmed dispute workflows are inside the assistant.
Five kept angles is useful, but the first data angle and contrarian efficacy angle partly overlap around the same two metrics: two-thirds handled and sub-2-minute resolution time.
gaps_in_B: "the Equivalent of 700 People Are Gone" is the worst line in either set. The update says the assistant handled 700 FTE-equivalent work, not that 700 people are gone.
"The Headcount It Cut Is the Margin It's Showing Investors" states a causal financial claim the facts do not prove. Klarna is profitable and headcount fell; that is not the same as AI-created margin.
"resolution time down 80%" is mathematically inferred, but B presents it as a supplied metric. Fine in analysis, sloppy in a headline-shaped angle without showing the calculation.
"every Bank and Payments Company Now Has a Public Benchmark" overreaches. The update gives Klarna's self-reported number, not an industry benchmark validated enough for every bank to measure against.
